 Odisha Cyclone Alert 2026 FAQs 
 Odisha Cyclone Alert 2026 is an emerging weather concern as a low pressure area over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal is forecast to intensify into a cyclonic storm by October 26, 2026. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned of heavy rainfall across Odisha, with the system expected to move towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. Authorities have initiated preparedness measures to minimise potential damage and protect coastal communities. 
 Odisha Cyclone Alert 2026 Latest News 
 As per the Bay of Bengal Cyclone update dated October 24, 2026, the developing weather system is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by October 26. The IMD has forecast very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall during the following days. Puri, Ganjam and Gajapati are among the districts highlighted for heavy rainfall warnings. The Odisha government has placed district administrations on high alert and arranged relief materials. 
 Odisha Cyclone October 2026 
 The expected Odisha Cyclone 2026 involves a developing low pressure system over the Bay of Bengal , with rainfall warnings and possible coastal impacts requiring close monitoring. 
 Formation and development: The low pressure area formed on October 23, 2026, under the influence of an upper air cyclonic circulation. It is forecast to develop into a depression on October 24, a deep depression on October 25 and a cyclonic storm by October 26. 
 Odisha Cyclone Date: October 26, 2026, is the forecast date for the system to intensify into a cyclonic storm.  
 Odisha Cyclone Path: The system is expected to move towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts around October 28, subject to changes in its movement. 
 Odisha Cyclone Name: The developing cyclonic storm is expected to be named as Cyclone Arnab . The name Arnab was proposed by Bangladesh and it applies if the system develops into the predicted cyclonic storm. 
 IMD Odisha Cyclone Warning: The IMD forecast indicates very heavy rainfall on October 27, extremely heavy rainfall on October 28 and very heavy rainfall on October 29 and 30. 
 Wind conditions: The developing system is forecast to bring stronger winds over the Bay of Bengal. Gale Winds of 70-80 km/h, gusting up to 90 km/h, were forecast from the morning of October 26, with hazardous conditions expected to continue until October 28. 
 Odisha Cyclone Live Updates: The IMD’s forecasts and official weather bulletins are the key sources for tracking the system’s movement, intensity, rainfall and potential coastal impacts. The exact landfall location has not been confirmed yet. 
 Affected Areas: The expected cyclone may affect coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh . In Odisha, Puri, Ganjam and Gajapati have been highlighted for heavy rainfall warnings. In Andhra Pradesh, coastal areas around Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam may require close monitoring as the system approaches. The exact areas likely to experience the strongest impacts will depend on the cyclone’s movement and updated IMD forecasts.

 Odisha Cyclone Tracker October 2026 
 The Odisha Cyclone Tracker 2026 helps residents monitor date wise IMD rainfall warnings, understand changing weather conditions and prepare for possible disruptions across affected districts. 
 October 24, 2026 – No Warning: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued no warning for this day under its seven day forecast. Residents should continue monitoring official weather updates. 
 October 25, 2026 – No Warning: The IMD has indicated no warning for October 25. People should remain attentive to subsequent advisories as the weather system develops over the Bay of Bengal. 
 October 26, 2026 – No Warning: No warning is listed for this date in the IMD’s forecast. However, the developing system is expected to intensify, making it important to follow updated official bulletins. 
 October 27, 2026 – Very Heavy Rain: The IMD has forecast very heavy rainfall across Odisha. Residents, particularly in vulnerable and low lying areas, should follow district level advisories and take precautions against waterlogging and flooding. 
 October 28, 2026 – Extremely Heavy Rain: The IMD has forecast extremely heavy rainfall, indicating an increased risk of flooding and severe waterlogging in affected areas. Residents should follow official safety instructions and prepare for possible disruptions. 
 October 29, 2026 – Very Heavy Rain: Very heavy rainfall is forecast by the IMD for this date. Communities should remain alert to local weather advisories and possible disruptions to transport, electricity and essential services. 
 October 30, 2026 – Very Heavy Rain: The IMD’s forecast continues to indicate very heavy rainfall. Residents should monitor updated warnings and follow instructions issued by local authorities as weather conditions evolve. 
 Odisha Cyclone Expected Impacts 
 The expected Odisha Cyclone may affect coastal and inland districts through intense rainfall, strong winds, flooding and disruption to transport, livelihoods and essential services. 
 Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall: Several districts may experience intense rainfall from October 26 onwards. Very heavy rainfall is forecast for October 27, extremely heavy rainfall for October 28 and very heavy rainfall for October 29 and 30. 
 Flooding and waterlogging: Persistent heavy rainfall may lead to waterlogging in urban areas and flooding in low lying locations. Agricultural fields, rural settlements and road networks could also face disruption depending on rainfall intensity. 
 Damage to infrastructure: Strong winds and heavy rain may damage houses, electricity lines, roads and communication networks. Such damage could interrupt essential services and delay relief operations in affected areas. 
 Impact on fishing communities: Rough seas and strong winds may threaten fishermen, fishing boats and other marine activities. The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the sea and those already at sea to return to the coast. 
 Disruption to agriculture and livelihoods: Heavy rainfall and flooding may affect standing crops, livestock and fishing related income. The extent of losses will depend on the storm’s final track, intensity and rainfall distribution. 
 Coastal safety concerns: Communities near the coastline may face weather related risks as the system approaches. Authorities may undertake evacuations depending on the cyclone’s intensity and the threat to life and property. 
 Odisha Cyclone Preparedness 
 Preparedness measures for the Odisha Cyclone Warning focus on timely warnings, coordinated administration, safe evacuation, emergency supplies and protection of vulnerable coastal communities. 
 District level readiness: The Odisha government has placed district administrations and departments on high alert. District collectors are responsible for coordinating local preparedness and requesting disaster response teams when required. 
 Relief material arrangements: The state government has stated that adequate relief materials have been arranged. These supplies are intended to support people who may require assistance during heavy rainfall and cyclone related emergencies. 
 Disaster response forces: The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) have been kept on standby. Their availability supports emergency response, rescue operations and relief work when required. 
 Cancellation of official leave: The government has cancelled the leave of officials. This measure aims to ensure administrative availability during the expected weather emergency. 
 Monitoring and public alerts: Residents should follow the latest official IMD warnings and district administration instructions. Updates on rainfall, wind speed, possible evacuation and local safety arrangements should guide decisions as the system develops. 
 Why is Odisha Prone to Cyclonic Storms? 
 Odisha’s location along the Bay of Bengal exposes its coastline to tropical cyclones , which are influenced by warm ocean waters, atmospheric conditions and seasonal storm tracks. The key reasons for the development of frequent cyclones in Odisha are: 
 Location along the Bay of Bengal: Odisha lies along a major cyclone corridor on India’s eastern coast. Storms developing over the Bay of Bengal can move towards its coastline, creating recurring exposure to strong winds and heavy rainfall. 
 Warm ocean waters: Warm sea surfaces supply heat and moisture that support tropical cyclone development. When atmospheric conditions are favourable, these disturbances can strengthen over the Bay of Bengal and move towards coastal regions. 
 Seasonal cyclone activity: October to December is an important period for cyclone activity in the North Indian Ocean . Odisha’s location makes it vulnerable to systems that approach the Odisha-West Bengal coastline during the post monsoon season. 
 Favourable atmospheric conditions: Cyclones develop when ocean heat, atmospheric moisture, a weather disturbance, sufficient rotation and relatively weak upper level winds combine. These conditions can allow a low pressure system to intensify into a cyclonic storm. 
 Storm movement towards the coast: Larger atmospheric wind patterns influence cyclone tracks. When these systems move west-northwestwards across the Bay of Bengal, Odisha and neighbouring coastal states may experience strong winds, heavy rainfall and associated hazards.

 Odisha Cyclone Alert 2026 FAQs 
 Q1. What is the latest Odisha Cyclone update for October 2026? + 
 Ans . As of October 24, 2026, a low pressure area over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal is forecast to intensify into a cyclonic storm by October 26. Heavy rainfall warnings are expected from October 27 onwards.
 Q2. What is the expected Odisha Cyclone date in October 2026? + 
 Ans . The system is forecast to become a cyclonic storm by the morning of October 26, 2026. Its movement towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts is expected over the following days, but the exact landfall location remains uncertain.
 Q3. What is the name of the Odisha Cyclone in October 2026? + 
 Ans . The developing Bay of Bengal Cyclone in October 2026 is expected to be named as Cyclone Arnab, a name proposed by Bangladesh. This name applies if the low pressure system develops into the predicted cyclonic storm.
 Q4. Which Odisha districts are under alert as per the IMD Warnings? + 
 Ans . Puri, Ganjam and Gajapati have been highlighted for heavy rainfall warnings. The supplied IMD schedule forecasts very heavy rainfall on October 27, extremely heavy rainfall on October 28 and very heavy rainfall on October 29 and 30.
 Q5. How can I track the Bay of Bengal Cyclone live? + 
 Ans . People can follow official IMD weather bulletins, cyclone forecasts and district administration advisories for updates on the storm's location, intensity, rainfall and wind conditions. Residents should rely on official warnings for safety decisions and follow evacuation instructions when issued.
